concepts.name: Tinkathia System: Structure and Mechanics
key_dimensions: Obligation to cultivate 3/20th (tinkathia = 3 kathas per bigha) of landholding with indigo
Distinction between tinkathia as a customary obligation vs. contractual imposition by planters
How the system evolved from voluntary to coercive practice under colonial land tenure
Difference between tinkathia and sharecropping (batai) — UPSC trap on conflating the two

concepts.name: Indigo Plantation Economy: Colonial Agrarian Structure in Bihar
key_dimensions: Role of European planters (neel sahibs) operating under long-term lease (zirat) arrangements
Shift from Bengal to Bihar as the indigo production center after the Indigo Revolt of 1859–60
How synthetic indigo (1897 German invention) undermined indigo economy yet planters continued exploitation via compensation levies
Distinction between indigo cultivation economics in Bengal vs. Champaran — different grievance structures

concepts.name: Abwabs: Illegal Cesses and Peasant Indebtedness
key_dimensions: Nature of abwabs — arbitrary levies beyond rent imposed by planters and landlords
Categories: tawan (advance/forced loan), lahna (compensation for switching from indigo), sairat (grazing rights levy)
Role of abwabs in perpetuating debt bondage — linking agrarian distress to credit exploitation
UPSC trap: abwabs were not legally recognized but enforced through social coercion, not the Bengal Tenancy Act

concepts.name: Gandhi's Entry into Champaran: Political and Strategic Significance
key_dimensions: Raj Kumar Shukla's role in persuading Gandhi — significance of peasant agency in initiating the movement
Gandhi's prior commitments at Lucknow Congress (1916) — timeline precision for Prelims
Why Gandhi chose Champaran over other agrarian distress areas — strategic value of a contained, localizable struggle
Contrast with Gokhale's advice to observe India for a year before acting — Gandhi's deviation and its implications

concepts.name: The Champaran Agrarian Inquiry Committee (1917): Gandhi's Method of Fact-Finding
key_dimensions: Gandhi's use of systematic peasant testimony as a political tool — precursor to satyagraha methodology
Government's initial order to Gandhi to leave Champaran and his deliberate defiance — civil disobedience framework
Composition of the official inquiry committee: Gandhi as member alongside British officials — significance of inclusion
Outcome: Champaran Agrarian Act 1918 — abolition of tinkathia, NOT immediate eviction of planters (common trap)

concepts.name: Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918: Provisions and Limitations
key_dimensions: Abolished the tinkathia system — made indigo cultivation purely voluntary
Provided for refund of illegal exactions (abwabs) — limited in practice due to evidentiary burden on peasants
Did NOT address the fundamental issue of land ownership by European planters or security of tenure
Distinction from Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 — Champaran Act was specific and remedial, not a comprehensive tenancy reform

concepts.name: Constructive Programme in Champaran: Beyond Agitation
key_dimensions: Establishment of schools in Barauli, Bhitharwa, Madhubani — Gandhi's integration of social reform with political struggle
Role of volunteers: Mahadev Desai, Narhari Parikh, Kasturbai Gandhi — team-based organizing model
Sanitation and health campaigns — linking peasant dignity to nationalist consciousness
UPSC angle: Champaran as the prototype for Gandhi's constructive programme later formalized in 'Constructive Programme' (1941 pamphlet)

concepts.name: Satyagraha as Political Method: Champaran as First Application on Indian Soil
key_dimensions: Distinction between passive resistance and satyagraha — Gandhi's own articulation post-South Africa
Three elements tested at Champaran: civil disobedience, non-cooperation with unjust orders, truth-force (satya + agraha)
Why Champaran succeeded where earlier petitionist approaches failed — shift from prayer to pressure
UPSC trap: Champaran is called Gandhi's 'first' satyagraha in India, but Bardoli (1928) and Kheda (1918) are often confused as earlier or simultaneous

concepts.name: Role of Local Leadership and Peasant Agency in Champaran
key_dimensions: Raj Kumar Shukla and Sheikh Gulab as grassroots mobilizers — importance of pre-existing peasant networks
Brij Kishore Prasad and Rajendra Prasad's legal support — interface between educated nationalist and peasant community
Peasant testimony as collective political action — subaltern voice within nationalist framework
Critique: Movement remained dependent on Gandhi's charismatic authority — limited autonomous peasant organization post-1918

concepts.name: Champaran vs. Kheda Satyagraha (1918): Comparative Agrarian Context
key_dimensions: Champaran: issue of forced cultivation and illegal levies; Kheda: issue of revenue demand during crop failure
Legal basis differs — Kheda invoked revenue rules on remission; Champaran challenged an extralegal customary system
Both in 1917–18 but different outcomes: Champaran had legislative resolution; Kheda ended with administrative concession
UPSC trap: Which was Gandhi's 'first' satyagraha in India — answer is Champaran (1917), Kheda is second

concepts.name: Colonial Land Tenure System in Bihar: Zamindari, Raiyati, and Plantation Overlap
key_dimensions: Three-tier structure: European planter → zamindar (often the same or in collusion) → raiyat (cultivator)
Bengal Permanent Settlement (1793) as structural backdrop — how it created conditions for planter exploitation in Champaran
Distinction between ryotwari and zamindari systems — Bihar under zamindari, which enabled tinkathia enforcement
UPSC angle: How Permanent Settlement, designed for revenue stability, inadvertently empowered intermediate exploiters

concepts.name: British Administration's Response: From Expulsion to Cooperation
key_dimensions: Lieutenant Governor's initial order to expel Gandhi — and Gandhi's non-compliance as a defining moment
Government's eventual capitulation and inclusion of Gandhi in inquiry committee — reasons: fear of wider unrest, WWI context
Role of WWI in shaping British response — India's loyalty sought; repressive measures politically costly in 1917
Commissioner's report vs. Gandhi's findings — how official and nationalist narratives diverged

concepts.name: Champaran and the Nationalist Movement: Integration of Agrarian Grievances into Congress Politics
key_dimensions: Pre-Champaran Congress attitude toward peasant issues — largely urban, elite, petitionist
How Champaran demonstrated that agrarian masses could be mobilized within nationalist framework
Gandhi's report to Congress — legitimizing peasant issues as national issues
Contrast with earlier peasant movements (Indigo Revolt 1859, Pabna Agrarian League 1873) that lacked nationalist umbrella

concepts.name: Synthetic Indigo and the Transition of Planter Exploitation Post-1897
key_dimensions: German synthetic indigo (BASF, 1897) made natural indigo commercially unviable — planters shifted strategy
Transition from tinkathia (forced cultivation) to tawan/lahna (monetary compensation levies) — exploitation continued in different form
Economic paradox: indigo cultivation became unprofitable yet peasants still coerced — rent extraction replaced crop extraction
UPSC trap: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) occurred ~20 years after synthetic indigo — movement was against residual exploitation, not peak indigo economy

concepts.name: Gandhi's Interaction with the Colonial Legal System in Champaran
key_dimensions: Gandhi's statement before the magistrate — 'I am here to serve the people, I cannot leave' — template for civil disobedience
Use of legal proceedings as a political platform — turning trial into testimony
Gandhi's simultaneous engagement with the inquiry as a legal/factual process and as a political mobilization
Precedent set for using colonial courts as sites of nationalist assertion — later used in Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience

concepts.name: Economic Condition of Champaran Peasants: Indebtedness, Tenure Insecurity, and Pauperization
key_dimensions: Multiple layers of obligation: rent to zamindar + indigo duty to planter + abwabs + moneylender interest
Occupancy rights under Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 — theoretically protected but practically undermined in plantation areas
Link between indigo cultivation obligation and food insecurity — land diverted from subsistence crops
Gandhi's inquiry data: documented evidence of economic distress as a political weapon — anticipates use of statistics in nationalist discourse

concepts.name: Champaran Satyagraha and Its Place in the Trajectory of Gandhi's Leadership
key_dimensions: Champaran as Gandhi's transition from 'returned South African activist' to 'all-India leader'
How Champaran shaped Gandhi's view on the relationship between local grievance and national liberation
Rajendra Prasad's account ('At the Feet of Mahatma Gandhi') as a primary source — historiographical significance
UPSC angle: Champaran is the bridge between Gandhi's South African satyagraha and the mass national movements of 1919–1942

concepts.name: Indigo Revolt of 1859–60 vs. Champaran Satyagraha 1917: Historical Continuity and Rupture
key_dimensions: Indigo Revolt: spontaneous, violent resistance in Bengal; Champaran: organized, non-violent, Gandhi-led in Bihar
Both targeted tinkathia-type obligations but different methods — highlights evolution of peasant protest strategies
Nil Darpan (1860) as propaganda tool vs. Gandhi's inquiry report — different modes of documenting and publicizing grievances
UPSC trap: Indigo Revolt was in Bengal (Nadia, Murshidabad); Champaran is in Bihar — different regions, different legal frameworks

concepts.name: Women's Participation and Social Reform Dimensions of Champaran Satyagraha
key_dimensions: Kasturbai Gandhi's role in running schools and conducting sanitation work — early model of women in constructive programme
Purdah system as a barrier to peasant women's participation — Gandhi's attempt to address through social reform alongside political action
Champaran as an early instance of linking caste/gender oppression to agrarian exploitation within nationalist framework
Limitation: women's political agency remained subordinate to Gandhi's organizational authority — critique from feminist historiography

concepts.name: Historiographical Debates on Champaran Satyagraha: Nationalist vs. Subaltern Perspectives
key_dimensions: Nationalist historiography (Rajendra Prasad, Tendulkar): Gandhi as liberator of passive peasant masses
Subaltern Studies critique (Shahid Amin's 'Gandhi as Mahatma'): peasants projected their own meanings onto Gandhi — he became a mythic figure, not just a political leader
Jacques Pouchepaddi's work on indigo economy — economic historian's perspective on structural causation
UPSC angle: Mains question may ask to 'critically assess' Champaran — requires awareness of both celebratory and revisionist interpretations
